intro: Fulltofta is a hamlet in Hörby municipality in central Skåne, in the south of Sweden, among farmland and woods north-east of Lund. A reader sent us one of its trees: a broad old oak at the edge of a wood, photographed bare in November, its long crooked limbs reaching out almost level over a bank of young birches. We do not know its girth or age yet, and we would like to.

trees.name: The Wide Oak of Fulltofta

location.address: Edge of a wood near Fulltofta, Hörby, Skåne

trees.story:
A reader sent us this oak from the edge of a wood at Fulltofta, in the farmland and beech country of central Skåne, photographed on a bright November day after its leaves had come down.

Bare, it hides nothing. A short, thick trunk rises out of a bank of scrub and, at about head height, breaks into great crooked limbs that run out sideways, almost level, before they turn upwards. Each of them divides again and again until the crown is a dark net drawn across the sky, far wider than the trunk would lead you to expect. Thin young birches stand all round its foot, pale and straight, and they make the old tree look even broader by comparison.

We do not know its girth, its age, or which of Sweden's two native oaks it is, pedunculate or sessile. A few brown leaves still hanging in the photograph are not enough to tell. If you stand under it with a tape measure, or know what the people of Fulltofta call it, tell us here and we will add your figures as yours.

Come in winter, as the reader did, when every limb stands clear against the light, and walk all the way round the trunk to see how far the branches reach.
trees.how_to_recognise: A broad old oak on a scrubby bank at the edge of a wood: a short thick trunk that splits at head height into long crooked limbs reaching out almost level, with thin young birches crowding its foot.
trees.access: Countryside near Fulltofta, Hörby. The reader walked up to it; we have not confirmed who owns the land. Sweden's right of public access lets you cross open land on foot, away from gardens and growing crops.
